Article.ArticleTitle: Risk Assessment and Monitoring of Antibody Responses to Biosimilars in Chronic Inflammatory Diseases.

Abstract.AbstractText: The expiry of the patent of several leading biological medicinal products has led to a surge in the development of 'biosimilar' products. In contrast to generic small-molecule medicines, biosimilars are not identical to their reference medicinal products.

Full comparability in quality as well as in preclinical and clinical issues is required to register a biosimilar. Since immunogenicity is key for biological medicinal products, regulatory authorities in the European Union require antidrug antibody (ADA) responses to be evaluated and to be approached from a safety perspective.

Marketing authorization in Europe has been granted for biosimilars of infliximab and etanercept and recently the Committee for Medicinal Products for Human Use has referred a positive opinion to the European Commission for two biosimilars of adalimumab. The availability of more sensitive and more drug tolerant ADA assays had led to an increased detection of ADAs, and hence new insights into the frequency of ADAs early in the course of treatment and into how these antibodies relate to clinical efficacy of the drug.

A phase I study, in which equivalence in terms of pharmacokinetics, pharmacodynamics, safety and immunogenicity between biosimilar and medicinal reference product has to be demonstrated, is followed by phase III clinical study to demonstrate no clinical meaningful differences with respect to efficacy, safety and immunogenicity. Depending on the immunogenicity risk identified and available measures to monitor and mitigate that risk, the testing program for immunogenicity may be less or more than that described in the general guideline.
